subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For WebChat sends targeting a Codex native thread that may be oversized or unrunnable, should Gateway fail/rotate before returning `started`, keep immediate ACKs with mandatory post-ACK recovery, or expose a separate health/recovery contract?
rationale: The central blocker is not a one-line defect: current docs promise immediate accepted ACKs, current source still ACKs before dispatch/transcript persistence, and changing that behavior can affect Gateway protocol and session-state semantics.

options.title: Pre-ACK Liveness Guard
options.body: Before returning `started`, prove the Codex thread can be used or rotate it, and return a visible error instead of accepting when no run can begin.

options.title: Post-ACK Recovery Contract
options.body: Keep immediate ACK semantics but require durable user-message persistence plus final error/lifecycle events whenever dispatch or Codex turn startup fails after ACK.

options.title: Health-First Recovery Surface
options.body: Leave send semantics mostly unchanged but add a visible stuck-thread health and repair path before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Pre-ACK Liveness Guard
recommendation.body: Before returning `started`, prove the Codex thread can be used or rotate it, and return a visible error instead of accepting when no run can begin.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the latest merged native Codex overflow mitigation that most directly intersects the reported oversized-thread state.
